articles.title: Eleições 2026: saiba como foi o dia do candidato André Luís ao governo do Maranhão | G1
articles.standfirst: André Luís cumpriu agenda na Ceasa e falou sobre medidas para integrar agricultura familiar, agronegócio, indústria e comércio no Maranhão.
articles.summary: André Luís cumpriu agenda na Ceasa e falou sobre medidas para integrar agricultura familiar, agronegócio, indústria e comércio no Maranhão.
articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão André Luís (Missão) e Orleans Brandão (MDB) cumpriram agenda de campanha nesta terça-feira (25) com foco na agricultura e no agronegócio. Eles apresentaram propostas para o setor durante as atividades do dia. O candidato Reginaldo Lima (PCO) não teve compromisso de campanha divulgado.

📲 Clique aqui e se inscreva no canal do g1 Maranhão no WhatsApp

A TV Mirante acompanhou os compromissos de campanha dos candidatos desse grupo e registrou as propostas apresentadas por cada um ao longo do dia.

Veja abaixo como foi o dia do candidato André Luís:

André Luís (Missão) — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Mirante

O candidato ao governo do Maranhão pelo partido Missão, André Luis, iniciou a agenda de campanha desta terça-feira (25) com uma visita à Central de Abastecimento (Ceasa), em São Luís.

Durante a manhã, ele conversou com feirantes e trabalhadores do local e ouviu demandas relacionadas à produção e comercialização de produtos agrícolas.

O candidato perguntou sobre os principais desafios enfrentados pelos trabalhadores e falou sobre propostas para ampliar a produção e a renda no campo.

Entre as medidas apresentadas por André LuiS está o investimento em estradas para melhorar o escoamento da produção agrícola. Ele também defendeu a integração entre agricultura familiar, indústria e comércio.

"Nossas propostas para a agricultura, agronegócio é conectar todas as pontas com único coração", afirmou o candidato.

André Luiz também propôs a unificação das secretarias de Agricultura Familiar, Abastecimento e Indústria e Comércio. Segundo ele, a medida teria como objetivo criar uma integração entre os setores e ampliar as oportunidades para produtores.

"A agricultura familiar precisa ser colocada no eixo do desenvolvimento por meio da indústria e comércio", declarou.

articles.title: Veja como foi o dia dos candidatos ao governo do Pi nesta terça (25) | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha de Elizeu Aguiar, Francisco Jurity, Geraldo Carvalho, Gustavo Henrique, Joel Rodrigues, Lúcia Santos, Lourdes Melo, Professor Gisvaldo, Rafael Fonteles, Ravenna Castro e Santiago Belizário.
articles.summary: Acompanhe as caminhadas, reuniões e propostas de Rafael Fonteles, Joel Rodrigues e outros candidatos ao governo do Piauí nas Eleições 2026 nesta terça-feira.
articles.body:
Eleições 2026: Candidatos ao governo no Piauí — Foto: Montagem/g1

Candidatos ao governo do Piauí realizaram caminhadas, visitas a apoiadores, entrevistas, reuniões, panfletagens, gravações para o horário eleitoral e encontros com diferentes setores da sociedade nesta terça-feira (25), em Teresina e no interior do estado.

O primeiro turno de votação será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato, em ordem alfabética:

Pela manhã, o candidato realizou gravações de vídeos para o período eleitoral e participou de sabatinas em rádio e TV. Dedicou a tarde a novas gravações de vídeos para o período eleitoral e a uma entrevista em programa de podcast.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou gravações de campanha nas proximidades da Praça do Liceu e concedeu entrevista a um programa de TV. No período da tarde, participou de uma reunião com a coordenação de campanha e de um debate online com apoiadores.

Durante a manhã, o candidato participou de uma caminhada por um trecho da Avenida Miguel Rosa, no sentido da Avenida Joaquim Ribeiro até a Avenida Nações Unidas, pelo lado direito da via. Em seguida, visitou o Mercado da Vermelha e o entorno, além de realizar gravações de conteúdos para as redes sociais.

No período da tarde, participou de uma reunião com a coordenação de campanha, realizou gravações para o horário eleitoral e fez corpo a corpo nas paradas de ônibus da Praça da Bandeira. Na sequência, reuniu-se com simpatizantes e apoiadores.

Durante a manhã, o candidato participou de uma caminhada pela Avenida Zequinha Freire. Durante a agenda, afirmou que a segurança pública será uma das prioridades do plano de governo e prometeu realizar concurso público para contratar 5 mil policiais militares .

“Há um compromisso nosso de contratar, através de concurso público, 5 mil para o efetivo da Militar, mas ampliar também a Civil, ampliar também a segurança dentro do Corpo de Bombeiro, Polícia Penal, mas principalmente a Militar, porque precisamos ter uma polícia presente nos bairros, não só no centro de Teresina, mas nos grandes centros em todos os bairros”, declarou.

Em seguida, realizou gravações para o programa eleitoral. No período da tarde, participou de uma reunião com a coordenação de agenda. Durante a noite, participou de reuniões com apoiadores nas proximidades da Associação dos Moradores do bairro Nova Brasília, no bairro Mocambinho e no espaço Remelexo, no bairro Vale Quem Tem.

Durante a manhã, a candidata concedeu entrevista a um portal de notícias e participou de uma reunião com a assessoria para alinhamento interno. A candidata não teve agenda durante a tarde.

Lourdes Melo não divulgou compromissos políticos marcados para esta terça.

Durante a manhã, a candidata concedeu entrevista a um portal de notícias. No período da tarde, visitou apoiadores e familiares na Zona Sul de Teresina, realizou panfletagem em praças do Centro da capital e participou da Assembleia Geral dos Trabalhadores dos Correios.

Pela manhã, o candidato realizou uma visita ao Parque Ambiental Floresta Fóssil. Em seguida, visitou o Encontro das Águas e estabelecimentos da região, além de participar de um encontro com ambientalistas e profissionais da área e realizar uma visita ao Polo Cerâmico. Dedicou a tarde a uma caminhada pelo Centro de Teresina e a uma reunião com a coorenação de campanha.

Iniciou a manhã em um café com apoiadores no Mercado do Mafuá. Durante a agenda, o candidato destacou a proposta do Pacto pela Economia, com foco no fortalecimento dos pequenos empreendedores , além de reafirmar compromissos com áreas como saúde, educação e segurança pública.

“É fundamental apoiar todos esses empreendedores de diversas formas, sobretudo com crédito, com infraestrutura, com o ambiente de negócio desburocratizado e qualificação. Isso é o que vai garantir mais sucesso desses pequenos empreendimentos e mais oportunidades para o nosso povo. É o que nós estamos chamando de Pacto pela Economia. Essa nossa visita aqui aos mercados de Teresina carrega também essa ênfase do nosso plano de governo em relação aos pequenos empreendedores. O foco é mais oportunidade de trabalho, emprego e renda, que é o eixo global do nosso plano de governo”, afirmou.

No fim da tarde, o candidato participou de um encontro com o setor empresarial.

Durante a manhã, a candidata cumpriu agenda administrativa. Durante a tarde, acompanhou o candidato ao Senado em uma visita aos trabalhadores vidraceiros de Timon. Em seguida, participou de uma visita à comunidade evangélica na Zona Sudeste.

Durante a manhã, o candidato visitou trabalhadores da limpeza urbana na Ladeira do Uruguai. Em seguida, realizou panfletagem no Mercado do bairro Satélite e no entorno.

Durante a tarde, participou de uma caminhada pelo bairro Mocambinho.

articles.title: Quaest em PE: veja como está a disputa pelo Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça (25) foi encomendada pela Globo. Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça (25) foi encomendada pela Globo. Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado em Pernambuco. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

✅ Receba no WhatsApp as notícias do g1 PE

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest, em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados, 80% estão indecisos, porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos. Veja os números abaixo:

A Quaest ouviu 1.302 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 21 e 24 de agosto. A margem de erro é de tês pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é PE-07828/2026.

Quaest: Raquel Lyra, 44%; João Campos, 36%

68% aprovam e 24% desaprovam governo de Raquel Lyra

Presidência em PE: Lula, 54%; Flávio, 19%; Caiado, 3%; Renan; 2%; Cury, 1%; Zema, 1%

Agora, veja os resultados que consideram apenas as respostas para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda.

Abaixo, veja os dados completos da pesquisa espontânea.

A Quaest perguntou também aos eleitores sobre cada um dos candidatos: se eles conhecem e votariam, se não conhecem ou se conhecem e não votariam. Os candidatos mais rejeitados (maiores índices de "conhece e não votaria") são Marília Arraes e Mendonça Filho.

Marília Arraes (PDT), Humberto Costa (PT), Mendonça Filho (PL) e Eduardo da Fonte (PP) — Foto: Arte/g1

articles.title: 'Robôs assassinos': ONU defende limites globais para armas capazes de atacar sem intervenção humana | G1
articles.standfirst: ONU e Cruz Vermelha pedem regras internacionais para armas capazes de selecionar e atacar alvos sem intervenção humana direta e alertam que o avanço da tecnologia está aumentando os riscos para civis.
articles.summary: ONU e Cruz Vermelha pedem regras internacionais para armas capazes de selecionar e atacar alvos sem intervenção humana direta e alertam que o avanço da tecnologia está aumentando os riscos para civis.
articles.body:
Um drone de ataque de longo alcance FP-1, da Ucrânia, é lançado em local não revelado do país, em 16 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: AP/Efrem Lukatsky

A Organização das Nações Unidas ( ONU ) e o Comitê Internacional da Cruz Vermelha (CICV) reforçaram nesta terça-feira (25) um apelo para que os países adotem proibições e limites ao uso de armas autônomas, sistemas que podem identificar e atacar alvos sem comando humano direto e que são frequentemente chamados de " robôs assassinos ".

🗒️Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Envie para o g1

O pedido dá continuidade a uma iniciativa lançada há três anos e às negociações internacionais que vêm sendo realizadas sobre o tema. As duas organizações não defendem uma proibição total de todas as tecnologias do tipo, mas pedem regras claras para controlar seu desenvolvimento e uso.

Embora afirmem que esses sistemas já estão sendo desenvolvidos, ONU e Cruz Vermelha dizem não ter confirmado seu emprego em combate.

As entidades argumentam que a criação de regras é necessária para proteger a população civil antes que esse tipo de arma passe a ser utilizado de forma mais ampla.

"Estamos perigosamente perto de cruzar uma linha moral: permitir que máquinas escolham seres humanos como alvos de forma autônoma", afirmou a porta-voz da ONU em Genebra, Alessandra Vellucci, ao ler uma declaração conjunta do secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, e da presidente do CICV, Mirjana Spoljaric.

No texto, os dois líderes afirmam que o alerta ganha ainda mais urgência agora. Segundo eles, as preocupações permanecem as mesmas, mas os riscos aumentaram.

A ONU e a Cruz Vermelha argumentam que o rápido avanço das tecnologias militares está colocando pressão sobre as normas internacionais existentes e ampliando a distância entre o que a tecnologia é capaz de fazer e o que a legislação consegue regular.

"As armas autônomas não pertencem a um futuro distante. A corrida para ampliar a autonomia dos sistemas de armas já está em andamento", diz a declaração.

O novo apelo ocorre enquanto diplomatas se preparam para uma reunião em Genebra, em novembro, dedicada ao fortalecimento da Convenção sobre Certas Armas Convencionais, acordo internacional que reúne países para discutir limites a armamentos considerados particularmente preocupantes.

A ONU e o CICV avaliam que esse fórum oferece o caminho mais concreto para a criação de regras internacionais obrigatórias sobre armas autônomas.

Os esforços para impor restrições a essas tecnologias vêm se arrastando há anos sem produzir resultados definitivos. O debate ganhou força à medida que drones e outros sistemas não tripulados passaram a ser usados em conflitos como a guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia, além de confrontos no Oriente Médio, no Sudão e em outras regiões.

Até agora, veículos robóticos terrestres têm sido empregados na Ucrânia principalmente para transportar equipamentos, levar suprimentos às tropas e retirar feridos do campo de batalha. A estratégia reflete a tentativa de reduzir a exposição de soldados em um cenário marcado pela presença crescente de drones.

Na avaliação da ONU e da Cruz Vermelha, os alertas não vêm apenas de organizações humanitárias. Cientistas e engenheiros envolvidos no desenvolvimento dessas tecnologias também têm defendido a criação de limites para seu uso.

O documento conclui dizendo que 2026 precisa marcar uma mudança de rumo nas negociações internacionais sobre o tema.

Embora afirmem que esses sistemas já estão sendo desenvolvidos, ONU e Cruz Vermelha dizem não ter confirmado seu emprego em combate.
As entidades argumentam que a criação de regras é necessária para proteger a população civil antes que esse tipo de arma passe a ser utilizado de forma mais ampla.

articles.title: Suspeito de cometer seis furtos, um roubo e uma violação de domicílio é preso em Boa Vista | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação aponta atuação em grupo para invadir casas do bairro Raiar do Sol, Operário e outros bairros na zona Oeste da capital; outro envolvido também foi detido por ordem judicial em aberto.
articles.summary: Investigação aponta atuação em grupo para invadir casas do bairro Raiar do Sol, Operário e outros bairros na zona Oeste da capital; outro envolvido também foi detido por ordem judicial em aberto.
articles.body:
Suspeito tinha pelo menos oito boletins de ocorrência — Foto: Polícia Civil/Divulgação

Um homem, de 23 anos, foi preso nesta segunda-feira (24), por uma série de furtos nos bairros Raiar do Sol, Operário e outros bairros próximos da zona Oeste de Boa Vista . A investigação identificou que o suspeito se envolveu em seis furtos, um roubo e uma violação de domicílio.

Além disso, a Polícia Civil (PC) prendeu um homem apontado como comparsa do investigado. Contra ele, havia um mandado de prisão em aberto por falta de pagar pensão alimentícia.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 RR no WhatsApp

De acordo com levantamentos dos policiais, o investigado costumava agir com outros envolvidos, pulando muros e invandindo casas, principalmente quando os moradores estavam ausentes.

O comparsa foi preso e conduzido para os procedimentos legais referentes ao cumprimento do mandado de prisão civil.

O suspeito de furto foi indiciado por furto qualificado. Após ser preso, ele foi conduzido à delegacia, onde a prisão preventiva foi formalizada. O investigado foi apresentado nesta terça-feira, 25, à Audiência de Custódia.

Leia outras notícias do estado no g1 Roraima .

articles.title: Illegal immigrant accused of fentanyl dealing linked to Virginia high school overdoses
articles.summary: Isaac Melendez-Carranza, an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, allegedly dealt fentanyl near Park View High School in Loudoun County, Virginia.
articles.body: An illegal immigrant from El Salvador who has faced a final deportation order since 2024 was caught and later released on bond at the Texas border in 2016 before his arrest last week for allegedly dealing fentanyl near a Virginia high school, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Isaac Melendez-Carranza, 31, was arrested Aug. 20 and charged with distributing fentanyl within 1,000 feet of a school. He is being held without bond at the Loudoun County Adult Detention Center. "ICE lodged a detainer on August 20 for Isaac Melendez-Carranza, an illegal alien from El Salvador, with the Loudoun County Jail," a DHS spokesperson told Fox News. An immigration judge issued Melendez-Carranza a final order of removal on July 18, 2024, according to DHS. THE BORDER IS CLOSED THANKS TO PRESIDENT TRUMP. IN VIRGINIA, THAT DOESN’T MATTER Melendez-Carranza was encountered in Sterling, Virginia, less than a month later, on Aug. 16, 2024, but no action was taken, DHS said. The department cited the Biden administration for the lack of action. U.S. Border Patrol arrested Melendez-Carranza near Hebbronville, Texas, on May 3, 2016, after he illegally entered the U.S. via the Rio Grande, according to DHS. He was released on bond on July 13, 2016, the department said. The Loudoun County Sheriff’s Office identified Melendez-Carranza as a suspected drug dealer connected to overdoses involving Park View High School students in May. MEXICAN NATIONAL FACES FEDERAL CHARGES AFTER CBP FINDS $238K IN FENTANYL INSIDE ELECTRIC MOPED Deputies seized about 100 pills and approximately $1,000 in cash during a search of his home, FOX 5 DC reported. Multiple students had been hospitalized following suspected overdoses at Park View High School in May, the outlet said. Loudoun County Public Schools confirmed at the time that two students suffered nonfatal suspected overdoses during school hours. Additional students were taken to a local hospital for evaluation after exhibiting symptoms, district officials said. The school system noted that it was unclear whether the incidents were connected and could not immediately confirm whether controlled substances were involved. JEANINE PIRRO CALLS OUT 'DIRTBAGS' AFTER 14 CHARGED IN ALLEGED COCAINE RING OPERATING FEET FROM A SCHOOLYARD Sheriff Mike Chapman called the case particularly alarming because the illicit drugs were reaching local students. The sheriff's office said Melendez-Carranza will be turned over to ICE after he is released, Fox 5 DC reported. "He’s here illegally," Chapman said. "I think he came in about 10 years ago. We shouldn’t be here and maybe if he wasn’t here this would not have happened, so we take that quite seriously. There is a detainer on him from ICE, so once he is done with his charges here, he will be released to ICE." The sheriff's office said more arrests are possible, but there was no timetable. Chapman confirmed ICE placed a detainer on Melendez-Carranza, who will be transferred to federal immigration authorities after his local criminal charges are resolved. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, ICE is targeting the worst of the worst. Nearly 70% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S.," DHS said.

articles.title: âUS not in economic position to further restrict, no one buys their bombastâ: Iran
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iranian Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has hit back at the United States over its escalating economic pressure on Tehr.
articles.body: Iranian Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has hit back at the United States over its escalating economic pressure on Tehran, saying Washington is not in a position to further restrict its economic relations with other countries.Ghalibafâs remarks came after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent launched âOperation Economic Outcastâ, a campaign aimed at cutting Iranâs financial links around the world and targeting countries and networks that continue to support Tehran economically.In a post on X, Ghalibaf said, "Americans know that no one buys their bombast; the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries.""Iran's trading partners, both in the media and through messages sent to us, have made it clear that they don't take these statements into account anywhere," he added.The latest exchange comes as Washington expands sanctions against Iran and seeks to restrict Tehranâs access to international financial networks, oil markets and other sources of revenue.Bessent warns Iran of global isolationBessent announced âOperation Economic Outcastâ on Monday, describing it as a broad campaign to sever Iranâs financial connections and cut revenue supporting the Iranian government and its military apparatus.The Treasury secretary said Washington had identified the networks Iran uses to move oil and evade sanctions."Treasury has mapped every node, facilitator, and network that Iran has used to smuggle oil and evade sanctions. Beginning today, the actions of Treasury and other agencies will block every potential source of revenue that funds the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the evil Iranian regime," Bessent said.He said Iran now faced a choice between international isolation and returning to the global economy."Iran now faces a clear choice, with only two paths before them: complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path to normalcy with the opportunity to rejoin the global economy. Today we are launching Operation Economic Outcast to foreclose all other options available to the Iranian regime," Bessent added.Bessent also directly addressed Iranian soldiers, urging them to question the consequences of continuing to support the government."To the ordinary soldiers supporting this regime, as more and more of your paychecks stop or are supposedly just delayed, ask whether your commanders are leading your country to triumph or to ruin," Bessent said."And recall that the Berlin Wall fell when ordinary soldiers decided not to shoot at their own people," he added.The Treasury secretary had warned a day earlier in an opinion article that an "economic D-Day is coming for Iran". His remarks followed similar calls from US President Donald Trump for greater economic pressure on Tehran and a return to negotiations.Washington targets Iranâs economic lifelinesThe latest US measures come after Washington imposed sanctions on nearly 60 Iranian individuals, entities and vessels linked to military activities, procurement networks and petroleum and petrochemical trade.The sanctions target Iranâs oil trade, shipping networks and military-linked organisations, including its so-called âdark fleetâ of tankers and international intermediaries accused of helping transport Iranian petroleum and petrochemical products.Washington has also targeted senior Iranian military figures and organisations accused of supporting Iranâs military operations and procurement activities.The State Department said the measures were intended "to further expose individuals and entities that enabled strikes against US forces and allies and to restrict the revenue that the Iranian regime uses to attack its neighbors, support terrorism abroad, brutally oppress its own people, and hold the global economy hostage."The sanctions form part of the Trump administrationâs broader effort to restrict Tehranâs access to international markets and financial networks.Tehran warns pressure could hurt diplomacyThe escalation has coincided with Iranian calls for diplomacy and greater regional engagement.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned on Monday that Washingtonâs approach could complicate diplomatic efforts. He made the remarks during a meeting with Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir in Tehran."The United States must correct its tone and approach in its interactions with Iran, because relying on coercion and bullying will only complicate the implementation processes," Pezeshkian said."Our nation will overcome any pressure and threat by relying on this solidarity," he added.Pezeshkian also called for greater cooperation between Iran, neighbouring countries and other Islamic nations, saying Tehran was ready to engage on economic, political and security issues."The Islamic Republic of Iran is ready for any cooperation and interaction in the economic, political, and security dimensions with Islamic countries and neighbours, because the Holy Prophet (PBUH) has always commanded peace and friendship," he said.He also stressed the importance of unity among Islamic countries amid continuing regional tensions."The unity and cohesion of Islamic countries is the most important deterrent against the conspiracies of the Zionist regime and the enemies of Islam, and if this convergence is realised, the enemies will not be able to advance their sinister goals," he said.Pakistan seeks role in de-escalationMunirâs visit to Tehran has added a diplomatic dimension to the growing confrontation between Washington and Tehran.The Pakistan Army chief held talks with Iranian officials and expressed support for greater bilateral cooperation. He also welcomed efforts aimed at advancing regional stability."In order to advance common goals and achieve a comprehensive agreement, it is essential that diplomatic processes be discussed and examined with complete precision and meticulousness," Munir said.He also described the countriesâ historical, religious and cultural ties as an asset in dealing with the current regional situation."The deep historical, religious and cultural commonalities between Pakistan and Iran are a valuable asset for overcoming the current complex circumstances and charting a bright future," he said.The latest developments underscore the widening gap between Washingtonâs economic pressure campaign and Tehranâs push for diplomacy. While the US seeks to cut Iranâs financial and oil revenues, Iranian officials have warned that further coercion could complicate efforts to reach diplomatic agreements.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Songs created by AI banned from Australia's music charts
articles.summary: The move comes weeks after a DJ admitted using AI to remix a Madonna song that topped the Australian charts.
articles.body:
Songs that are largely or wholly created by AI have been banned from Australia's music charts.

From this week, all releases must be "substantially human made" to be eligible.

The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said the new code would help "promote the human nature of artistry".

It follows a controversy around a cover of Madonna's Like A Prayer by Australian DJ Josh Fawaz which recently topped the ARIA dance singles chart and peaked at number 2 on the country's overall chart.

The song has become a staple of commercial radio station playlists and been streamed more than 48 million times on Spotify alone.

Fawaz later added generative AI credits to the song after a backlash.

ARIA said that Australian artists were competing for attention "in the most crowded market in history" and that it was "not interested in promoting or celebrating the success of AI-generated music that does not contain human artistry".

Under the new rules, AI assistance can still be used, but humans must have written the song, and have performed the lead vocal and primary instruments.

AI can also still be used for mastering songs and, for example, using drum machines and auto tune.

Earlier this year a song was banned from Sweden's music charts because it was created by AI.

And in July, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said AI guidelines would be rolled out in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia for use in their official charts.

The updated code, based on the IFPI directive, also excludes music that raises "stream or chart manipulation concerns".

ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd said: "These changes reflect our intent to remain dynamic and promote the human nature of artistry in what is, to say the least, a rapidly developing space."

"Artists already use AI tools in their work, the charts can and should evolve to keep room for that, but music generated wholesale by services built on artists' recordings is a different matter."

She added: "A chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent."

Artists will be required to declare AI use when they submit a song for chart consideration.

ARIA said that if it later emerged music was largely AI-generated it could retrospectively adjust chart positions, and if the piece topped the charts, it may request that awards given for reaching Number One were returned.

Artists and their representatives will be able to challenge their exclusion.

Among the artists supporting the move are Australian electronic act Peking Duk.

Last month, they shared an AI-assisted version of their 2014 hit High on Instagram, captioned: "When you re-record your own song with AI so Australian radio will play it."

Band member Adam Hyde told Channel Nine's Today show that AI-generated music was "removing the human experience from life".

In July this year, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese promised "the strongest possible protection" from AI for Australian creatives.

Albanese pledged that writers and musicians would be able to choose if and how their work was used in the training of AI, saying it would be "theft" if creatives lost that control and were not paid for its use.

How can you tell if your new favourite artist is a real person?

Spotify to add label for AI-generated artists and remove them from recommendations

And in July, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said AI guidelines would be rolled out in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia for use in their official charts.
The updated code, based on the IFPI directive, also excludes music that raises "stream or chart manipulation concerns".
ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd said: "These changes reflect our intent to remain dynamic and promote the human nature of artistry in what is, to say the least, a rapidly developing space."
"Artists already use AI tools in their work, the charts can and should evolve to keep room for that, but music generated wholesale by services built on artists' recordings is a different matter."
She added: "A chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent."
Artists will be required to declare AI use when they submit a song for chart consideration.

ARIA said that if it later emerged music was largely AI-generated it could retrospectively adjust chart positions, and if the piece topped the charts, it may request that awards given for reaching Number One were returned.
Artists and their representatives will be able to challenge their exclusion.
Among the artists supporting the move are Australian electronic act Peking Duk.
Last month, they shared an AI-assisted version of their 2014 hit High on Instagram, captioned: "When you re-record your own song with AI so Australian radio will play it."
Band member Adam Hyde told Channel Nine's Today show that AI-generated music was "removing the human experience from life".
In July this year, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese promised "the strongest possible protection" from AI for Australian creatives.

Albanese pledged that writers and musicians would be able to choose if and how their work was used in the training of AI, saying it would be "theft" if creatives lost that control and were not paid for its use.

articles.title: Goat sanctuary purchases 16.9 acres of more land in Kent
articles.summary: The land purchased by Buttercups Sanctuary for Goats will enable it to house up to 160 goats.
articles.body:
A goat sanctuary in Kent has purchased an additional 16.9 acres of land, which it said would enable it to house up to 160 goats.

Buttercups Sanctuary for Goats in Boughton Monchelsea said that the new plot of land was close to where it was currently situated and would provide "long-lasting results for both our adorable residents and the wider, beautiful countryside".

Matt Huggins said that it was the "most significant step since the charity's foundation".

"It's been something we've all been dreaming of for a long, long time, and we're all very excited to get going," Huggins added.

According to the sanctuary, the purchased plot of land had historically been used for agriculture and will enable it to rescue more goats and double its on-site capacity.

It said a lot of work would need to be carried out on the land despite being a "blank canvas", but new goats are expected to begin living there by spring 2027.

Huggins added that its long-term vision included solar panels, wind turbines and habitat networks for the wildlife, which he expected would take years to be fully completed.

"There's a long road ahead, and we are going to need the help of our supporters to make it a final reality, but we've taken the first major step," he said.

articles.title: Jersey earnings rise by 1.2% after inflation
articles.summary: Statistics Jersey says the increase is "slightly lower" than the long-term annual average.
articles.body:
Average earnings in Jersey did not keep up with the rate of inflation for the year to June, according to new figures.

Statistics Jersey said in June 2026 earnings per full-time equivalent employee was 4.1% higher than in June 2025.

However, once adjusted for inflation - currently at 2.8% for the island , external - Statistics Jersey said earnings rose by 1.2%, representing a real-terms pay cut.

The Index of Average Earnings June 2026 report , external said the overall increase was lower than the preceding five-year annual average of 5.6% per year and "slightly lower" than the long-term annual average of 4.2% per year for 1991 to 2025.

It also highlighted average earnings in real terms increased by 0.9% in the private sector and 2.9% in the public sector over 12 years.

However, it said, over 25 years, average earnings in real terms in the public sector decreased by 3% while they increased by 1.2% in the private sector.

Statistics Jersey said the report was determined from earnings data collected from a large representative survey of employers and all Government of Jersey departments.

It said this was the fourth year in which the survey was compulsory for employers to complete.

Matthew Gill, a statistician for Statistics Jersey, said, when looking back at figures going back to 2001, there had not been much a change in real-term earnings.

He said: "It's not necessarily that people are earning less.

"With inflation going up, it is generally something that people will notice more.

"A lot of the inflation recently has been things like petrol, which people notice when topping up their cars and has an effect on deliveries for food and that type of thing."

Heidi Gibaut, executive director at Law At Work, said a lot of the firm's clients had taken on secondary roles to boost their income.

She said: "When I was younger, I did two roles; but it's not a sustainable way of living.

"It's not how you will get the best out of the colleagues that you currently work with."

Gibaut said she felt it was down to employers to make sure the services and products they offered were being done at the right price to stop inflation from getting worse and "ensure colleagues are paid well".

"But it is a really, really hard balance," she added.

articles.title: Russian stadium says it won't host Kanye West gigs
articles.summary: Two planned concerts are thrown into doubt, but Russian promoters insist they will go ahead.
articles.body:
The Russian stadium that was scheduled to host two shows by Ye, the rapper also known as Kanye West, has said the events will no longer take place.

In a social media post , St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said no rental agreement had been signed with the concert promoters. "Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site."

West would have been the first major Western performer to play Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The rapper is trying to rehabilitate his image after years of antisemitic remarks, for which he recently apologised.

Gazprom Arena acknowledged it had received complaints about West's planned appearance and stressed that it "was not and is not" responsible for his booking.

The stadium said in its statement that the sold-out concerts, scheduled for 10 and 11 October, had been organised by the Moscow-based Say Agency.

Posting on its Telegram channel, Say Agency said the stadium's announcement had come as a surprise.

"We learned about [it] at the same time as you did, through the media," the agency wrote. "As of now, the Ye concert has not been canceled," it added in a follow-up message.

"We are trying to contact the venue to find out the reason for the post and resolve the issue. We will keep you updated."

The BBC has contacted West's publicist for a comment on the uncertainty over his Russian shows.

In its statement, Say Agency said it announced the concerts earlier this month based "on an official letter that was approved by" Gazprom Arena.

The stadium subsequently sent a rental agreement, Say Agency claimed, and the agency acknowledged the contract had not yet been signed but said the deadline to do so did not expire until later this week.

Last week, Gazprom Arena had posted enthusiastically about the concerts on social media, calling Ye "the most influential musical artist of our time".

Fans reacted to its latest announcement with disappointment.

"This was the shortest concert of my life," responded one, under Say Agency's Telegram post. "It's a shame that the government is putting obstacles in your way," added another.

There is no indication that authorities intervened in the shows, but there has been opposition to West's booking from some Russian politicians.

Vitaly Milonov, a notorious conservative lawmaker, suggested the star should perform traditional Russian songs instead of his planned setlist, reflecting the anti-Western views of many nationalists.

"Maybe after this he'll stop his disgusting antics and become a normal person," Milonov added in a video statement.

West's antisemitic remarks began in 2022, when he made a series of offensive comments on social media that led to his accounts being suspended. Fashion brands like Adidas and Balenciaga also ended their relationships with the star.

The musician went on to declare he was "a Nazi", releasing a song called Heil Hitler and selling T-shirts featuring the swastika.

This January, West apologised in a full-page advertisement in the Wall Street Journal, writing: "I am not a Nazi or an antisemite."

Reflecting on a "four-month-long manic episode of psychotic, paranoid and impulsive behaviour", he said he was "deeply mortified" by his actions and that his bipolar disorder meant "you're manic [and] you don't think you're sick".

However, some questioned the timing of his statement - which coincided with the release of a new album, Bully, and the start of his world tour.

He held his first major concert in the United States in more than five years in Los Angeles in April, but planned shows in England, France, Italy and Poland have been cancelled over his past behaviour.

Say Agency acknowledged the controversy in a Telegram post last week , but defended its decision to bring West to Russia.

"Not everything Kanye West said should be forgotten," it said.

"Many people are talking about Kanye today. Many are trying to criticise him for words spoken during difficult times.

"But it's easy to judge based on a single statement. It's more difficult to listen to a person who has been changing the industry for decades. We listened, and we want to remind you."

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur complete the signing of Savinho
articles.summary: Tottenham Hotspur have completed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho in a reported £85 million deal.Spurs are said to be paying an initial £75 mill...
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur have completed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho in a reported £85 million deal.

Spurs are said to be paying an initial £75 million for the 22-year-old with a further £10 million to potentially be paid in add-ons.

"It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here," the Brazilian said on his arrival.

"It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

"As soon as I spoke to the Head Coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team."

Savinho first joined City in a controversial transfer from fellow City Football Ground club Troyes , after having never featured for the French side.

In total, Savinho featured 84 times for City during his time at the club, scoring seven times and making 13 assists.

articles.title: In 1959, Vermont bought Snake Mountain land but the seller kept timber rights; 67 years later the state plans to secure 949 acres of those rights and add 256 acres
articles.summary: US News: A conservation story that began nearly seven decades ago is entering a new chapter in Vermont. What was once a complicated split between land ownershi.
articles.body: A conservation story that began nearly seven decades ago is entering a new chapter in Vermont. What was once a complicated split between land ownership and timber rights at Snake Mountain is now set to be reunited, potentially giving wildlife, forests and outdoor enthusiasts greater protection for generations to come. According to media reports, with support from the Trust for Public Land, the Vermont Fish & Wildlife Department plans to secure the timber rights covering 949 acres of the Snake Mountain Wildlife Management Area (WMA). The state also plans to acquire an additional 256 acres in Addison and Weybridge, expanding the popular natural area by nearly 25%. It is reported that both transactions are expected to be completed by early 2027.A major expansion for Snake MountainLocated between Addison and Weybridge, Snake Mountain WMA currently encompasses 1,215 acres of forested landscape surrounded largely by farmland. Its proximity to some of Vermontâs largest population centres makes it an especially valuable place for people seeking access to nature. The planned 256-acre addition would expand the protected area while improving habitat connectivity. The project is also expected to create new opportunities for hiking, hunting and wildlife watching. The effort will simultaneously reunite the stateâs ownership of the land with the timber rights covering much of the WMA, allowing Vermont Fish & Wildlife to take a more coordinated approach to managing the landscape.Why timber rights matterWhen Vermont purchased the lands that became Snake Mountain WMA in 1959, the seller retained the timber rights. This meant that while the state owned the land for conservation and public access, responsibility for growing, managing and harvesting timber remained with the private owner. Such arrangements have historically been relatively common on Vermont Fish & Wildlife properties. More than six decades later, the state is seeking to bring those interests together. Acquiring the timber rights would allow Vermont Fish & Wildlife to coordinate forestry decisions with its broader goals for wildlife, recreation, water quality and habitat protection. Any future roads or skid trails required for timber harvesting could also be planned alongside conservation priorities.A haven for wildlifeSnake Mountain is far more than a scenic hiking destination. The WMA contains eight types of wetlands, including a glacial bog estimated to be about 9,500 years old. Its forests and wetlands provide habitat for a remarkable range of species. Peregrine falcons nest on the mountainâs western cliffs, while mature trees provide roosting habitat for federally endangered Indiana bats and northern long-eared bats. The landscape also supports woodland mammals, game birds, songbirds, amphibians and other wildlife. Protecting and connecting these habitats could become increasingly important as environmental conditions change.Building climate resilienceConservation groups say the expanded and reunified property could play an important role in climate resilience. The larger protected landscape would provide additional lowland forest habitat while helping safeguard wetlands and headwater streams. These interconnected natural areas can serve as important refuges for biodiversity and help species adapt as the climate changes. For a forested landscape surrounded by farmland, strengthening those connections could be particularly valuable.How the project is being fundedThe timber rights and additional acreage are being purchased from The A. Johnson Co., LLC, with funding assembled from local, state, federal and private sources. The project includes a $1.35 million grant from the US Fish & Wildlife Serviceâs Recovery Land Acquisition Grant programme, funded through the Land and Water Conservation Fund. It also includes $417,500 from the Vermont Housing & Conservation Board, support from the Town of Weybridge Conservation Fund and significant private donations. The availability of federal funding is linked largely to the habitat provided by Snake Mountain for endangered bat species.A long history of conservationThe A. Johnson Co. has managed the timber rights at Snake Mountain for decades. The company has maintained that responsible forestry can coexist with wildlife habitat, recreation and healthy natural communities. The planned transfer marks an opportunity to bring those long-standing conservation and forestry interests under unified management. Vermont Fish & Wildlife officials say the agency is particularly appreciative of the stewardship that helped maintain the quality of the landscape over the past several decades.More land could soon join the WMASnake Mountainâs expansion may not end with the 256-acre acquisition. In 2026, the WMA is also expected to receive a donation from The Nature Conservancy consisting of two adjoining parcels totalling 88 acres in Addison. Known as the Willmarth Woods Natural Area, the property contains one of the Champlain Valleyâs largest low-elevation mature forest stands. The area features rich soils supporting a high-quality mesic red oak and northern hardwood forest. It also contains the trailhead for one of the main hiking routes leading to Snake Mountainâs summit. Planned as an addition to Snake Mountain WMA since 1992, Willmarth Woods could further strengthen the ecological and recreational value of the protected landscape.Image Courtesy: istockCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner jailed after prostitution arrest
articles.summary: Jed York pleaded no contest to two charges in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.
articles.body:
Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York has been jailed in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.

The 45-year-old, who is also the owner of the San Francisco 49ers, was convicted of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after pleading no contest to two charges.

In the Ohio legal system, a no contest plea means a defendant accepts a conviction without formally admitting guilt.

York was sentenced to one day in jail on each offence, to be served concurrently, and was given credit for time already served.

York was fined $150 for disorderly conduct and $1,000 for possessing criminal tools.

Court records show the case was brought by East Palestine Police Department and filed at Columbiana County Municipal Court on Monday.

York pleaded no contest to both charges at an arraignment hearing and was found guilty.

Court records also show an expungement request was filed and denied on the same day. This is a request to have records destroyed or sealed so they are not accessible to the public.

According to reports in the US media, other court documents say York responded to an advertisement on a prostitution website placed by undercover officers from a Human Trafficking Task Force in Ohio.

These documents say he arranged to have sexual activity with a woman in exchange for $140 (£103).

In a plea deal, the original charge was reduced to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools - thought to refer to the phone used to reply to the advert.

The 49ers were part of the US consortium who took control of Rangers last year but York is not involved in the day-to-day running of the club.

Rangers and Leeds have both said they will not be commenting.

The 49ers said: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

York became a co-owner of Rangers through 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm linked to the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, where he serves as chief executive and principal owner.

In May 2025, a consortium led by US businessman Andrew Cavenagh and 49ers Enterprises completed a takeover of Rangers after acquiring a controlling 51% stake in the Scottish Premiership club.

Cavenagh became Rangers chairman, with 49ers Enterprises taking a leading role in the club's ownership.

The takeover followed months of negotiations and brought Rangers under majority American-backed ownership.

49ers Enterprises first invested in Leeds United in 2018 when the club was in the Championship, steadily increasing its investment as the Whites returned to the Premier League following a 16-year absence, before assuming full control in 2023.

As an NFL owner, York is subject to league policies. "We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL said.

What could Rangers expect from potential 49ers takeover?

Court records also show an expungement request was filed and denied on the same day. This is a request to have records destroyed or sealed so they are not accessible to the public.
According to reports in the US media, other court documents say York responded to an advertisement on a prostitution website placed by undercover officers from a Human Trafficking Task Force in Ohio.
These documents say he arranged to have sexual activity with a woman in exchange for $140 (£103).
In a plea deal, the original charge was reduced to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools - thought to refer to the phone used to reply to the advert.
The 49ers were part of the US consortium who took control of Rangers last year but York is not involved in the day-to-day running of the club.
Rangers and Leeds have both said they will not be commenting.
The 49ers said: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."
York became a co-owner of Rangers through 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm linked to the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, where he serves as chief executive and principal owner.
In May 2025, a consortium led by US businessman Andrew Cavenagh and 49ers Enterprises completed a takeover of Rangers after acquiring a controlling 51% stake in the Scottish Premiership club.
Cavenagh became Rangers chairman, with 49ers Enterprises taking a leading role in the club's ownership.
The takeover followed months of negotiations and brought Rangers under majority American-backed ownership.

49ers Enterprises first invested in Leeds United in 2018 when the club was in the Championship, steadily increasing its investment as the Whites returned to the Premier League following a 16-year absence, before assuming full control in 2023.
As an NFL owner, York is subject to league policies. "We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL said.
What could Rangers expect from potential 49ers takeover?

articles.title: Iran used mosques to surveil, shoot at January protesters: Report
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iranian security forces used mosques across Tehran as bases to deploy personnel, monitor protesters and confront demonstrators during a deadly crackdo.
articles.body: Iranian security forces used mosques across Tehran as bases to deploy personnel, monitor protesters and confront demonstrators during a deadly crackdown in January, according to evidence obtained by Iran International.Intercepted radio communications, video footage and eyewitness accounts reviewed by Iran International point to security operations being conducted from several mosques in and around the Iranian capital on January 8 and 9, when large crowds took to the streets.The report said security personnel discussed deploying forces and equipment inside Imam Hossein Mosque, which Iran International geolocated to the intersection of Sattari Highway and Mokhbari Street in western Tehran. Witnesses described security activity around the mosque after electricity was cut in the area, while surveillance drones flew overhead.According to Iran International, witnesses said security personnel positioned outside some mosques engaged protesters before forces inside emerged to beat and arrest demonstrators. The evidence, the report said, suggests that some mosques functioned not merely as places of worship or gathering, but as operational bases from which security forces monitored and confronted protesters.One witness told Iran International that several people were positioned on the roof of a mosque near Kashani Boulevard in western Tehran on January 8.The reported crackdown came amid widespread protests in Iran, as authorities faced growing public anger and unrest. The unrest has since been overshadowed by the broader conflict involving Iran, Israel and the United States, with the country now facing intense military and economic pressure.Nearly six months into the war, Washington has shifted towards economic pressure, with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announcing new sanctions against nearly 60 Iran-linked entities and warning countries doing business with Tehran to cut financial ties or face retaliation.âWe are level-setting with every country to tell them our expectations. We know who they are. They know who they are,â Bessent said.Iran's rial has also fallen to a record low, while rising prices have added to pressure on ordinary people. Yet the economic strain has not so far translated into significant political pressure on Tehran.At the same time, Pakistan has sent a high-level delegation to Iran to encourage Washington and Tehran to return to negotiations, underscoring the continuing uncertainty surrounding the conflict.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Obsessive' Billie Piper stalker Philip Jerome jailed
articles.summary: Philip Jerome admits breaching a stalking prevention order designed to protect the ex-Doctor Who star.
articles.body:
An "obsessive" fan with a "sexual interest" in Billie Piper has been jailed for 12 months for breaching a stalking prevention order designed to protect the ex-pop singer and Doctor Who star.

Philip Jerome, of Winchester, Hampshire, appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on his 49th birthday after pleading guilty to four breach charges.

The court heard police carried out an inspection of his devices on 27 December, finding four images of Piper saved on his phone, and that he had tagged 11 posts and images on X relating to her on four days that month.

Defence lawyer Caroline Bonavia said he had had a recent autism diagnosis and had sought psychological support over "obsessive" relationships.

The court was told Jerome had been made subject to a restraining order in 2018 after attending Piper's home address, posting cards through her door and sending letters by post to her.

He then breached the order in December that year by sending messages on Facebook to her mother and sister "expressing a wish for them to meet up" as well as for attending Piper's home and making comments about her choice of partner.

Police also found ring binders at his home containing newspaper clippings, details of events and other merchandise, the court heard.

Jerome was jailed for 12 months in 2022 for a breach of the restraining order by turning up at a Comic-Con convention where he posed for a photograph with Piper twice on the same day.

Security ejected him from the event after Piper had recognised him on the second occasion, the court was told.

The defendant had also been convicted of harassment against a female friend dating back to 2012 by "sleeping outside her address in the woods".

Prosecutor Anisa Alrubaie told the court Jerome had been made subject to the stalking prevention order relating to Piper on 21July 2022.

Alrubaie said one of the posts found during the police inspection of his devices on 27 December last year included a single comment on 7 December in which Jerome wrote that a GQ awards image might have made him fall for the star, adding: "She is great without a bra too."

The prosecutor said Piper's X account was organised by her personal assistant who did not "generally inform Ms Piper of posts" due to a "significant amount of negativity that is not relevant" of which she did not "need to be made aware".

District Judge Kirsty Allman told Jerome he had "demonstrated an entrenched pattern of stalking and harassment offences, and failing to comply with court orders".

The judge told Jerome the "motivation" was to contact Piper "in the hope she will engage in a relationship with you".

More stories from Hampshire & the Isle of Wight

Listen to the latest news from Hampshire and the Isle of Wight

Bonavia, defending, said: "Were it not for the order, these [offences] would be very similar to what a keen fan would post about a public figure.

"A lot of them are similar images of her head in an Andy Warhol arrangement, many repeats essentially of her face and sometimes with artificial intelligence (AI).

"The difference for him is that he must not do this and he accepts it."

Bonavia said Jerome had shown a lack of remorse and empathy, had had a recent diagnosis of autism and had sought psychological support to stop him seeking "obsessive and unsuccessful relationships".

She said his breaches "had moved a great deal away from what one would think were the terrifying elements".

"He needs to learn that fan or not, even this sort of posting is not permitted."

articles.body:

The average 30-year fixed rate is 6.63% , down 1 basis point since yesterday. The 15-year fixed loan is currently at 5.95% , 7 basis points higher than yesterday. The 5/1 ARM is 6.62% , 12 basis points lower than on Monday.

A mortgage calculator can help you see how various mortgage term lengths and interest rates will affect your monthly payments. Use this mortgage calculator to explore different outcomes.

You can bookmark the Yahoo Finance mortgage payment calculator and keep it handy for future use, as you shop for homes and lenders. It also considers factors like property taxes and homeowners insurance when calculating your estimated monthly mortgage payment. This gives you a better idea of your total monthly payment than if you just looked at the mortgage principal and interest.

30-year vs. 15-year fixed mortgage rates

Generally, 15-year mortgage rates are lower than those for 30-year mortgages. When comparing 15- versus 30-year mortgage rates , know that the shorter term will save you money on interest in the long run. However, your monthly payments will be higher because you're paying off the same loan amount in half the time.

For example, with a $400,000 mortgage with a 30-year term and a 6.19% rate, you'll make a monthly payment of about $2,447.28 toward your mortgage principal and interest. As interest accumulates over decades, you'll end up paying $481,021 in interest.

If you get a $400,000 15-year mortgage with a 5.65% rate, for example, you'll pay about $3,300.26 monthly toward your principal and interest. However, you'll only pay $194,047 in interest over the years.

If that 15-year mortgage payment is too high, remember you can always make extra payments on your 30-year loan to pay it off faster and ultimately pay less interest.

Fixed-rate vs. adjustable-rate mortgages

With a fixed-rate mortgage , your rate is locked in from day one. However, you will get a new rate if you refinance your mortgage.

An adjustable-rate mortgage keeps your rate the same for a specified period. Then, the rate will increase or decrease depending on several factors, such as the economy, and the maximum amount your rate can change according to your contract. For example, with a 7/1 ARM, your rate would be locked in for the first seven years, then adjust annually for the remainder of your term.

Adjustable rates sometimes start lower than fixed rates, but once the initial rate-lock period ends, you risk your interest rate going up. ARM rates have also been starting higher than fixed rates recently, so you may not always get a rate break.

Learn more: Determine how to choose between an adjustable-rate vs. fixed-rate mortgage

articles.title: Map shows countries paying people to have babies as birth rate drops
articles.summary: In one country, children can receive up to $55,000 by the time they turn 17.
articles.body:
Governments around the world are increasingly offering cash payments, tax breaks, housing subsidies and childcare support in an effort to persuade citizens to have more children as birth rates fall and populations age.

Declining birth rates can strain a country's economy because there aren't enough people being born to support the aging population. That means greater strains on social programs like Social Security and Medicare in the United States since more and more people are using the programs, but not enough people are paying into them. Declining birth rates are a global problem, and a growing number of countries are rolling out increasingly generous pro-family incentives, ranging from direct payments for newborns to years of childcare assistance.

Singapore has spent years expanding financial support for families as it grapples with one of the world's lowest fertility rates. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently announced a major expansion of family support measures, emphasizing that the government wants to provide assistance well beyond a child's birth and into the early years of parenting.

Each child will receive almost S$70,000, the equivalent of about $55,000 USD, in direct financial support by the time they turn 17. The program will replace the current program, which includes the Baby Bonus Scheme.

Under the Baby Bonus Scheme, parents are given cash gifts throughout the first six-and-a-half years of a child's life. The first and second child get a total of S$11,000, equivalent to about $8,660 USD, disbursed in six-month increments, and every other child gets S$13,000, equivalent to about $10,236 USD.

Under the Large Families Scheme, which will also be replaced when the new package goes into effect, families can receive an additional $16,000 for each third or subsequent child born after February 18, 2025.

Despite those efforts, Singapore's birth rate remains among the lowest globally. The cash incentives began in 2001 and haven't been able to reverse the declining trend in birth rates.

"Ultimately, the decision to have children is a deeply personal one. Policies alone cannot make this happen. But what we can do is make it easier for Singaporeans who want children to start and raise a family," Wong said in a statement.

China has dramatically shifted from restricting births to actively encouraging them.

After decades of the one-child policy, Chinese officials are now trying to boost fertility as births have fallen and the population has begun shrinking. In 2025, Beijing rolled out a nationwide childcare subsidy that provides families with 3,600 yuan, or about $500, annually for each child under age three.

The subsidy is part of a broader campaign to encourage childbirth and ease the cost of raising children. Chinese authorities have also supported local initiatives that offer even larger payments, including monthly stipends and bonuses for families with multiple children.

"International practices show that cash subsidies are an indispensable part of pro-birth measures," Zhang Benbo, a researcher at a think tank under the National Development and Reform Commission, said in a statement at the time.

The national program is expected to benefit millions of households each year and reflects mounting concern over China's aging population and shrinking workforce.

Japan has become one of the world's most prominent examples of a nation battling demographic decline.

The country's aging population and persistently low fertility rate have prompted officials to expand financial support for families. Government measures include monthly child allowances, a childbirth lump-sum grant that has been increased to 500,000 yen, equivalent to $3,139 USD, and expanded childcare services.

Japan is also launching new childcare and education support initiatives in 2026. These reforms aim to reduce the financial burden of raising children by expanding access to childcare regardless of employment status and broadening financial assistance for families. While unveiling a policy to promote people having kids in 2023, Children's Policies Minister Masanobu Ogura said the next few years are possibly "a last chance" for Japan to change the trajectory of its declining birth rate.

"While diverse views about marriage, childbirth and childrearing should be respected, we want to make a society where young generations can marry, have and raise children as they wish," Ogura said, according to the Associated Press. "The basic direction of our measures to tackle low births is to reverse the trend of declining births by supporting individuals' pursuit of happiness."

Officials have repeatedly said the country's future economic strength depends in part on stabilizing population trends.

South Korea has spent billions of dollars attempting to increase what has frequently been ranked as the world's lowest fertility rate. The government offers an extensive package of benefits that includes monthly allowances for parents, direct birth grants, childcare support, expanded parental leave and housing assistance.

South Korea launched a program in 2022 that gave mothers 2 million won, the equivalent of about $1,500 USD, when they gave birth and then an additional 700,000 won, equivalent to about $500 USD, each month until their child turns one. Then, parents get 350,000 won, equivalent to about $260 USD, per month until they turn 2.

A major South Korean company is also offering its employees incentives to have kids. The Lotte Group, a massive conglomerate, gives employees with three or more children a free 7-9 seat family vehicle, and housing group Booyoung offers employees a $75,000 bonus for each new child they have.

"Korea will face a crisis of national existence 20 years from now, including a decline in the economically productive population and a shortage of defense personnel to ensure national security and maintain order," Booyoung chairman Lee Joong Keun told CBS News in 2024.

South Korea is still struggling with its birth rate, but the number of babies born in South Korea increased in 2024, the first time in nine years.

Sweden doesn't pay a cash bonus for having kids, but provides parents with a monthly allowance depending on the number of children they have. Each eligible child is given 1,250 SEK, the equivalent of $132 USD, and families with two or more children are eligible for the Large Family Supplement.

Parents with two kids receive an additional 150 SEK per month, equivalent to $15 USD; three-child families get 730 SEK, equivalent to $77 USD; four-child households get 1,740 SEK per month, equivalent to $183 USD, and families with five or more children get an extra 1,250 SEK per month per child, equivalent to about $132 USD.

The country offers generous paid parental leave, subsidized childcare and income support designed to make balancing careers and family life easier.

Estonia has combined direct payments with broader family support programs aimed at encouraging larger families.

Parents receive childbirth allowances and other child-related benefits, with support increasing for households with multiple children. The country also offers paid parental leave and childcare policies that policymakers say help reduce the cost of raising children.

Families with one or two eligible children receive 80 euros per child per month, equivalent to $93 USD, and families with three or more eligible children receive 100 euros per child per month, equivalent to $116 USD. The payments are made to parents until children turn 19.

Estonia's family policy has long been cited internationally as an example of how financial assistance can be paired with social programs to support parents. Government officials have repeatedly emphasized that encouraging family formation requires both direct financial support and practical assistance.

Estonia's birth rate has been on the decline since 2021. The child allowance started in 1992.

Finland has adopted a combination of cash benefits and family support services to encourage child-rearing. One of the country's most famous family programs is the baby box, which provides new parents with essential supplies for newborns. Families can also receive financial assistance and monthly benefits.

Parents of eligible children receive monthly payments until the child turns 17. Families with one child receive 94.88 euros, equivalent to $110 USD, 104.84 euros for the second child, 133.79 euros for the third child, equivalent to $156.11 USD, 173.24 euros for the fourth child, equivalent to $202.15 USD, 192.69 Euros for the fifth child, equivalent to $224.84 USD.

Despite being family-friendly, Finland has one of the lowest birth rates among the Nordic countries.

"So we cannot really any longer say that it's our good family policies that explain good fertility in the Nordics," Anneli Miettinen, a research manager at Kela, told NPR in 2025.

The United Arab Emirates offers some of the most generous childbirth-related financial support programs available to citizens.

Emirati families can qualify for substantial financial assistance tied to childbirth, while lower-income households may also receive monthly child allowances. Additional benefits are available for larger families, including support related to housing and debt relief.

Depending on where a person lives, a UAE native citizen can receive up to AED 220,000, equivalent to about $60,000 USD, after the birth of their child.

One of the country's notable programs includes the NAFIS child allowance initiative, which provides monthly payments for eligible children. These policies are designed to reduce family expenses and encourage population growth among Emirati citizens. Families can get AED 600 per qualifying child each month, equivalent to $163 USD.

The benefits generally apply only to UAE nationals rather than expatriate residents, reflecting the government's focus on supporting citizen families.

Can Cash Incentives Reverse Falling Birth Rates?

While governments continue expanding family benefits, researchers remain divided on how much direct financial incentives can raise birth rates.

Studies have found that generous payments and childcare support can influence family planning decisions, particularly when combined with broader policies that reduce the long-term cost of raising children. Data show that it can cause an immediate bump, but often doesn't fix long-term population declines. As fertility rates remain below replacement levels across much of the developed world, policymakers are increasingly experimenting with new approaches.

Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Gray R. Thomas
